note: Closed set of violated-contract families. Every .github/failure-classes/FC-*.json names one in 'family'. Prefer reusing a class in the same family before declaring a new class; add a family only in a registry-only PR. Mirrors the quality-ladder escape-metric basis (omi-knowledge-base projects/backend-target-architecture/metrics/escapes/basis.json, version 2026-11-16.2).

families.state-single-owner: One durable writer and one derivation per piece of state; copies or re-derivations disagree.
families.write-fence: A stale, late or retried writer overwrites newer state (missing generation/revision fence, tombstone-first).
families.fleet-scope-bound: A per-process dedupe, lease, cursor, cache or limit is treated as a fleet-wide guarantee.
families.work-bounded-resumable: A timeout, budget or cap does not actually bound the work, discards in-flight work, or leaves an unbounded keyspace/TTL.
families.retry-classification: Deterministic failures retried forever or transient failures made terminal; queue redelivery used as recovery; poison loops.
families.txn-purity: Provider I/O, metrics or side effects inside a retryable transaction body.
families.deadline-budget: Per-hop timeouts instead of an end-to-end deadline; budgets with the wrong scope.
families.identity-qualifier: An id compared or stored without the qualifier that makes it unique (scope, owner, account generation, device).
families.destroy-after-quiescence: Delete, release or free before durable custody or before the last in-flight writer is quiescent.
families.projection-contract: A server verdict (processing/failed/settled/visible) re-derived by clients or composers instead of rendered from one contract.
families.cross-boundary-contract: Two ends of an interface (enqueue vs worker, rendered manifest vs API, generated client, SDK vs server) disagree.
families.duplicated-implementation: The same logic exists in several paths or languages and a fix did not reach all of them.
families.flag-binding: Flag off does not stop the work, flag not bound to the serving deployment, parsing bug, untested off path, unenforced prerequisite flag.
families.config-value-change: A capacity, cohort, budget or routing value change shipped without a ramp step, dose-response check or prerequisite.
families.derived-inventory: A hand-maintained list, allowlist, budget or count drifts from the code or races between branches.
families.test-fidelity: A fake, mock or fixture encodes the wrong contract, or a test does not assert the property it is named for.
families.ci-merge-integrity: Test selection misses the owning test, a shared shard hangs, merged on red, merge race on main.
families.deploy-prerequisite: A deploy-time IAM grant, secret, resource or manifest field is first exercised in production.
families.observability-gap: An alert or metric is missing, paused, unowned, unable to fire, or mislabelled, so the defect lived longer.
families.mitigation-attribution: A mitigation or rollback applied without causal attribution, later undone.
families.vendor-platform-behavior: External provider, OS, store, browser or hardware behavior differs from our model of it.
families.product-intent: The product rule was ambiguous or decided only after the change shipped.
families.ui-surface-contract: A UI surface breaks its interaction, layout, accessibility or platform contract (gestures, focus, chrome, localization rendering).
families.temporal-correctness: Clocks, time bases, time zones or ordering by time are wrong or taken from the wrong authority.
families.input-tolerance: Input parsing, encoding or normalization rejects valid input or accepts invalid input at a boundary.
families.security-privacy-boundary: Credentials, secrets, personal data or authority leak across a scope, log, cache or tenant boundary.
families.resource-lifecycle: A resource, task, subscription, cache entry or handle is not released, or outlives its owner.
families.spend-authorization: Paid work (model, STT, vendor calls) runs without the authorization or once-only guarantee that should bound it.
families.other: None of the above; give a short violated contract in violated_contract.
